source.title: An Empirical Study of Memorization in NLP

page_placements.theme: Example-specific memorization can help valid rare or difficult examples

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests memorization and its relationship to generalization with self-influence scoring and removal of high-scoring NLP training examples, but does not train models on random labels or perform the specified random-labeling intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper's own removal and attribution results concern self-influence/memorized instances and test accuracy. It does not report experiments on completely random labels, shuffled or noise inputs, label-noise fractions, explicit regularizers, or learning real versus random labels over training. Results cited from Zhang et al. (2017), Arpit et al. (2017), and Feldman and Zhang (2020) are not this study's rows.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Zhang et al. and Arpit et al. for memorization capacity, but its own experiments measure self-influence, atypicality, and test accuracy after removing naturally labeled examples. These results do not test random-label fitting, unstructured-input fitting, or the temporal ordering of learning real and noisy labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' long-tail conclusion: they interpret atypicality and removal experiments as validating the theory on three NLP datasets and showing that memorization can help generalization. Their conclusion also emphasizes their attribution method as a tool for understanding memorization and potentially improving models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses self-influence based on influence functions and removes high-scoring instances to test effects on test accuracy; it does not reproduce random-label training. NLP models use Distil-BERT with the word embedding layer and first four transformer layers frozen; CIFAR-10 uses pretrained ResNet50 features and a trained MLP classifier.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset/task changes which analyses are available: quantitative typicality is reported for SST-2, manual inspection for SNLI, and no typicality judgment for Yahoo! Answers; the test-accuracy removal comparison is reported across SST-2, Yahoo! Answers, SNLI, and CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: High-self-influence examples tend to be atypical in SST-2 and in qualitative inspection of SNLI examples (Section 3.2, Tables 1–3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-influence identifies atypical naturally labeled training examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing high-self-influence examples reduces test accuracy more than random removal across three NLP datasets and CIFAR-10. On SST-2, removing the top 30% yields a reported 1.44 percentage-point drop versus 0.70 for random removal (Section 3.3, Figure 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retaining high-self-influence training examples can benefit generalization on naturally labeled data.

fits_no_version.finding: Attribution-selected token or feature masking reduces self-influence more than random masking; qualitative examples highlight features atypical of their class (Sections 3.4–3.5, Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization attribution can locate features contributing to self-influence.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2022)
record.problems: No random-label or unstructured-input experiments, so the requested claim versions are not tested. The study reports one checkpoint for self-influence ranking; only SST-2 is used to compare rankings across three seeds. Test-accuracy curves are described in the text and shown in figures, with five retraining runs and standard deviation bars, but exact values are not supplied for most dataset/fraction combinations.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results for the specified claim versions; the study's instance-removal and token-attribution outcomes concern a different intervention and measure and therefore are not catalog rows for these versions.

untested.parts: All parts: fitting completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
All parts: relative training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
All parts: fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
All parts: perfect training fit and progressively worsening test error across random-label corruption fractions.
All parts: regularizers' effects on random-label fitting and generalization after their removal.
All parts: learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels over training.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate. Self-influence is a different operationalization of memorization from random-label interpolation. Class-atypical features do not establish label corruption or when those features are learned. The out-of-scope results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Randomly relabeled training sets, training/test error under random labels, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time or convergence rates for random labels and corrupted-label fractions.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep over random-label corruption fractions with training and test error.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their removal on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work cite Zhang et al. and Arpit et al. for memorization capacity without testing the random-label claim versions.

tranche.reason: Experiments examine self-influence, atypicality, removal of naturally labeled examples, and memorization attribution; none tests or uses V1–V6.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase matches Section 5. The long-tail memorization findings concern a different construct from V1–V6.

statements.correction: Section 3.3, Figure 1: SST-2 test-accuracy drop after removing the highest-self-influence 30% of training examples: about 1.44 percentage points; random removal of 30%: 0.70 percentage points. Results average five retraining runs.
